messages:
maria: Heads-up - after last night's RBAC cleanup we got alerts from proxy telemetry in eu-west that showed a spike in cert fetch latency and a small mTLS handshake failure rate.
josh: any customer-facing errors?
maria: only internal svc-to-svc retries and a handful of 502s from the proxy. no user-facing outages yet.
kevin: I pulled KMS audit and see a bunch of `PermissionDenied` on Decrypt around 00:12 UTC. looks tied to the cleanup.
anika: which binding was removed?
maria: the prune removed `group:infra-keystore-readers@redwood.com` from `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` across several projects.
kevin: snippet from keystore logs: ```
2026-03-08T00:12:17Z keystore ERROR fetch_cert: decrypt failed: rpc error: code=7 desc="Permission denied"
2026-03-08T00:12:17Z proxy WARN cert-fetch failed, aborting handshake
```
josh: so keystore couldn't decrypt key material, returned 500, proxy couldn't complete mTLS. fallback to TLS reported?
maria: yes. proxies dropped to TLS fallback for some inter-service paths. handshake metrics: mTLS success rate 98.9% -> 97.2% for ~10m.
anika: mitigation options? quick rollback or targeted grant?
kevin: prefer targeted grant to the specific SAs used by keystore proxy. rollback of group binding is fastest but broad.
sre-oncall: thresholds to declare incident? our policy is >1% mTLS failure sustained 10m -> P1. we were at 0.85% peak for 9m, trending down.
josh: immediate plan: 1) grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `serviceAccount:keystore-proxy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` scoped to the key resource, 2) enable an alert for KMS decrypt DENY spikes, 3) add RBAC prune dry-run check.
maria: I'll open a permissions PR for the scoped SA binding and ping infra-admin.
anika: also check if a key rotation coincided - if a new key-version was created it would explain decrypt attempts.
maria: looked at key versions - no rotation during the window. older key versions still valid.
kevin: create quick detection query for audit: ```
logName: "projects/redwood/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"
protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.status.code=7
```
maria: added a temporary alert rule and a dashboard panel for: KMS decrypt denies, keystore fetch errors, proxy mTLS fallback by region.
sre-oncall: please add a graph for ocsp/ct anomalies too. if cert chains shift some clients may hard-fail.
anika: I found one OCSP error in proxy logs: `OCSP responder error: no_revocation_info` but internal CA policy tolerates missing stapling for now. still, worth listing in postmortem.
josh: postmortem action items: - record RBAC diff and PR id - map which groups/services relied on removed binding - add CI dry-run for RBAC prunes that affect SA/group members interacting with KMS - scope keystore SA permissions and rotate keys if needed - add permanent alert on KMS decrypt denies.
kevin: long-term mitigation: implement `iam.simulate` check in the prune pipeline: `gcloud iam policies-simulate --principal=... --permission=cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` for affected principals. block prune if any return allowed=false for expected calls.
maria: agree. also add runbook snippet: detect KMS deny -> identify principal from audit -> check recent IAM changes -> if RBAC prune, either restore binding or bind scoped SA and notify oncall.
anika: I'll follow up with infra-admin to change the prune logic to keep groups referenced in `prod-keystore` allowlist.
josh: who owns postmortem? maria + anika. assign and set 48h deadline.
security-bot: [alert] KMS decrypt deny spike mitigated - monitoring for 24h.
maria: updating thread: PR created for scoped SA grant -> infra-admin review requested. will update when approved. :thumbsup:
